item.title: [ponylang/ponyc] 0.77.0
item.description:
ponylang/ponyc | 6200 stars| 440 forks.

| C++ | C | GAP | Shell | Pony | CMake | Dockerfile | PowerShell | Python |

Pony is an open-source, actor-model, capabilities-secure, high performance programming language

Use forward slash as the path separator on all platforms

All paths in the files package now use / as the separator on every platform, including Windows. Paths from Path.cwd() and Path.canonical() are /-separated, Path.sep() returns "/" unconditionally, and Path.clean() converts \ to / on Windows.

Path.is_sep() still accepts \ on Windows for parsing external input. Use Path.to_os() when a backslash path is needed for Windows shell commands.

Path.normcase() now only lowercases the path on case-insensitive platforms. It no longer replaces / with \ on Windows.

Before:

if path == "C:\\Users\\me\\project" then
  // ...
end

After:

if path == "C:/Users/me/project" then
  // ...
end

Code that passes paths to Windows shell commands should use Path.to_os():

let os_path = Path.to_os(path)

Remove Path.from_slash and Path.to_slash

Path.from_slash() and Path.to_slash() have been removed. All paths use / as the separator on every platform, so these functions served no purpose. Remove any calls to them.

Fix iftype specialization on method-level type parameters

When a method had its own type parameter with an iftype specialization guard, the compiler selected the specialized body unconditionally — even when the concrete type argument did not satisfy the guard. Class-level type parameter guards were not affected.

primitive Foo
  fun bar[S: ReadSeq[U8] box](seq: S): U16 ? =>
    (seq(0)?.u16() << 8) or seq(1)?.u16()

  fun bar[S: ReadSeq[U8] box](seq: S): U16
    iftype S <: Array[U8] box
  ? =>
    seq.read_u16(0)?

Calling Foo.bar[WrappedSeq](seq)? would fail to compile with "can't find a compatible 'read_u16' method on type 'WrappedSeq ref'" because the compiler chose the Array[U8]-specialized body instead of the default.

Fix match without else in trait default method always taking the first arm

A match without an explicit else in a trait default method body always took the first capture arm, regardless of the runtime type of the matched value. The first capture arm always ran, which could crash the program or silently produce wrong results when the matched value was a different type.

trait T
  fun get(): (R | None)

  fun check() =>
    match get()
    | let r: R => r.n  // always taken, even when get() returns None
    end

The same match written in a class body, or with an explicit else, worked correctly.

Remove the classic pool allocator

The pool_classic, pool_retain, and pooltrack build options are removed. The arena allocator, the default since 0.69.0, is now the only full allocator. pool_memalign remains for builds that need AddressSanitizer or Valgrind.

Builds that used pool_classic,valgrind should switch to pool_memalign,valgrind:

Before:

cmake --preset debug -DPONY_USES=pool_classic,valgrind

After:

cmake --preset debug -DPONY_USES=pool_memalign,valgrind

Builds that used pool_classic on its own should drop it — the default arena allocator is what runs.

Fix subtype checking for intersections that collectively satisfy an interface

The compiler rejected an intersection type (A & B) as a subtype of an interface when neither A nor B alone provides every method the interface requires, even when together they cover all of them.

interface Sized
  fun rows(): USize
  fun cols(): USize

class HasRows
  fun rows(): USize => 10

class HasCols
  fun cols(): USize => 20

primitive Checker
  fun check(s: Sized) => None

  fun example(x: (HasRows & HasCols)) =>
    check(x) // previously rejected: neither HasRows nor HasCols alone is Sized

The call check(x) failed with a subtype error because the compiler checked each intersection member individually. It now checks the intersection's members collectively against the interface's method list, so (HasRows & HasCols) is accepted as a subtype of Sized.

Detect locals and parameters that shadow inherited methods

The compiler now reports an error when a local variable or parameter reuses the name of a method inherited from a trait or interface. Previously, only methods defined directly on the type were checked — inherited methods were silently shadowed, which could hide the inherited method and cause unexpected behavior.

Locals and parameters that shadow inherited methods are now a compile error

Code that previously compiled may now fail if a local variable or parameter has the same name as a method inherited from a trait or interface. Rename the variable or parameter to fix the error.

Before:

interface Tickable
  fun label(): String => "default"

class MyTimer is Tickable
  fun format(label: String): String =>
    "Timer: " + label

After:

interface Tickable
  fun label(): String => "default"

class MyTimer is Tickable
  fun format(msg: String): String =>
    "Timer: " + msg

Fixed

  • Fix iftype specialization on method-level type parameters (PR #6292)
  • Fix match without else in trait default method always taking the first arm (PR #6297)
  • Fix subtype checking for intersections that collectively satisfy an interface (PR #6304)
  • Detect locals and parameters that shadow inherited methods (PR #6305)

  • Use forward slash as the path separator on all platforms (PR #6276)
  • Remove Path.from_slash and Path.to_slash (PR #6276)
  • Use forward slash as the path separator on all platforms (PR #6276)
  • Remove the classic pool allocator (PR #6301)

item.title: [kemalcr/kemal] v1.15.0
item.description:
kemalcr/kemal | 3926 stars| 206 forks.

| Crystal | HTML |

Fast, Effective, Simple Web Framework
  • (SECURITY) Never route a request-target that does not start with /, and refuse a malformed one (GHSA-x97g-6h7h-q9w6). The route key is the method followed by the path with nothing in between, so the request line GE T/admin/secret built the key of GET /admin/secret and was served by that route, while every path-scoped guard read T/admin/secret and stood aside: use "/admin", Auth, before_all "/admin/*", a Kemal::Router mounted at /admin, prefix only/exclude rules. Any verb worked - DELET E/admin/users/42 ran the delete route. Such a request is now answered 400 Bad Request with Connection: close, through a registered error 400 like the refusal of a malformed method (#820). The route tree, context.route and the only/exclude rules of a Kemal::Handler no longer resolve a method and a path that cannot both be believed, so a handler that answers by itself behind only ["/metrics"] no longer served GE T/metrics - nor GET/metrics /, which the method check of #820 left reaching it. Absolute-form (http://host/path), authority-form (CONNECT host:port) and OPTIONS * targets are well formed, routed nowhere and still get 404.
  • (SECURITY) Run Kemal::Router filters for every request the router's routes serve, ws routes included (GHSA-89xc-29wg-6mm5). A router's filters were registered by path only for its HTTP and SSE routes, so a router.before or router.before_get authentication guard let a WebSocket handshake to the same router through - an unauthenticated client reached the ws handler, also under namespace and mounted sub-routers. Registering them by path also let filters elsewhere decide whether they ran, and a filter path was compared with the spelling of the router's route paths, so a guard could silently not run for HTTP routes too. Router filters now travel with the router's routes, and a filter path is matched against the request path (router.before "/users/:id" covers a get "/users/me"). Thanks @barisern for the report 🙏
  • (BREAKING) Filters around a WebSocket handshake, following the fix above:
    • The GET filters run for a handshake - top-level and router, including a pathless before_get, which therefore runs on every handshake. A filter that assumes an HTTP route, such as env.route.path, raises there.
    • A filter refuses a handshake with halt, or with a status a registered error handler covers; the refusal closes the connection. A status alone still upgrades, as it still runs an HTTP route's handler.
    • after filters do not run for a handshake, since they would run once the 101 is on the wire - also where an HTTP route shares the path, which used to run them.
  • (BREAKING) A router's filters apply to the router's own routes only. A top-level route or ws on the same path no longer runs them; guard it with top-level filters. For a request no route serves, the router before filters of a route on the path still run, so a router guard or CORS preflight answer keeps covering the methods the router does not serve. Router filters run after the top-level filters of the same step.
  • (BREAKING) Run every top-level path filter whose path matches the request, in the order their paths were first registered, instead of only the most specific one. Global filters (before_all and friends without a path) still run first, router filters last. Before upgrading, check the filters whose paths overlap:
    • A more specific filter path no longer exempts its paths from a broader guard. With before_all "/api/*" { halt 401 unless authenticated } and any before_all "/api/login" filter, POST /api/login used to get past the guard and now answers 401. Skip such paths inside the guard itself, e.g. next if env.request.path == "/api/login".
    • Filters on overlapping paths all run, so side effects such as logging, counters or rate limits may run more than once per request: before_get "/admin" next to before_get "/admin/" both run for either spelling, since each matches both. One block registered for several paths at once, as with before_all ["/admin", "/admin/*"], still runs once.
    • The filter on the path registered later has the last word. before_all "/api/html" { |env| env.response.content_type = "text/html" } followed by before_all "/api/*" { |env| env.response.content_type = "application/json" } now answers /api/html with JSON; register the more specific path after the broader one. A block added to a path later joins that path's place, so registering /api/html again after /api/* does not help. after filters run in the same order, not reversed.
    • Why: path filters shared one radix tree that ran the single best match, so a broader guard silently did not run wherever a more specific filter path matched too: with before_all "/api/*" { halt 401 } and before_all "/api/public" { ... }, GET /api/public skipped the guard and got 200, and before_get "/users/:id" was skipped for GET /users/me once before_get "/users/me" existed. A filter path now matches what it matches on its own: the shared tree could also lose filters altogether, so before_get "/users/:id" and before_get "/users/:uid/posts" together ran for neither /users/5 nor /users/5/posts, and it refused some combinations at boot with Radix::Tree::SharedKeyError - add before_get "/users/me" to those two - which are now accepted. Kemal::FilterHandler#tree no longer holds the path filters.
  • (BREAKING) Run no before filter after one that closed the response with halt or redirect - not later blocks on the same path, path filters after a halting before_all, the before_get step after the before_all one, or router filters - just as it already kept the route handler from running. after filters still all run. Before upgrading:
    • A before filter that has to see refused requests - audit logging of failed logins, a metrics counter - no longer runs for them when it comes after the guard. Move it to an after filter.
    • Refuse with halt. A guard that only sets a status for a registered error handler leaves the response open, so the filters after it still run and can change the status.
    • An after filter that sets a header or the content type has to check env.response.closed? first: on a halted response it raises IO::Error, which skips the after filters behind it, after_all logging included.
    • Why: the filters after a halt kept running on a response already sent. With before_all "/api/*" { halt 401 } and before_get "/api/public" { |env| env.response.content_type = "application/json" }, the client got its 401 but content_type= raised IO::Error on the closed response, which skipped after_all, and a later filter's work - a database lookup, a counter - ran for a request the guard had refused. With overlapping path filters now all running, a halting guard with a filter behind it is the common case.
  • End the connection when an exception arrives after the response headers have gone out, instead of reading the next request on it. Kemal::ExceptionHandler could no longer render an error page at that point and returned as if the request had succeeded, so under keep-alive the server answered the next request on the same connection. A route that set Content-Length: 100, flushed partial and raised had the next pipelined response spliced into the 93 missing bytes - partialHTTP/1.1 200 OK... - which a client, or a proxy pooling the connection, read as one body. The connection now closes after the cut, as it does when an exception escapes the handlers altogether, so the client sees the response end short (curl: (18) end of response with 93 bytes missing). A chunked response, which the server still ends with its final chunk, and a response halt already closed keep their connection - an after filter touching a header of a large streamed response (#759) costs nothing. An error page for an exception raised before anything is sent is unchanged.
  • Leave a request path that names no static file to the routes instead of redirecting it. StaticFileHandler runs ahead of the routes and compared the decoded path with its canonical form, so an encoded / or a byte that is not UTF-8 in a route param never reached the route: with get "/u/:id", /u/a%2F%2Fb answered 302 /u/a/b and /u/%FF answered 302 /u/%EF%BF%BD. A non-canonical path is now redirected only when it names a file under public_folder, or when it has a . or .. segment - so /u/..%2F..%2Fetc still answers 302 /etc and no route receives a dot segment the handler would have resolved away.
  • Fix content_for in a partial rendered with render "partial.ecr" inside render(view, layout). The partial was rendered into a String::Builder, and its block kept writing into that builder, which had already been turned into the partial's string by the time the layout's yield_content ran the block. So <% content_for "meta" do %><title>From partial</title><% end %> in a partial left <%= yield_content "meta" %> empty, and the late write grew the finished builder, freeing the memory behind the string the partial had returned: a view that kept that string and printed it after yield_content sent whatever the heap held there - route keys, CLI option names - instead of the partial. A content_for block now receives the buffer yield_content collects it in as an argument, so the block reaches the layout from a partial as it does from the view, and a partial is rendered into an IO::Memory, so its string can no longer be overwritten.
  • Honour If-Range in send_file and the static file handler, per RFC 9110 §13.1.5. A Range was served whenever it parsed, so Range: bytes=0-3 with If-Range: "stale-etag" or If-Range: Mon, 01 Jan 2001 00:00:00 GMT got 206 and the first bytes of the current file, which a resuming client appended to the prefix it had of an older one, corrupting the download silently. A Range is now only honoured when If-Range names the response's validator: an entity tag by strong comparison (so Kemal's weak W/"..." tags never match), a date only when it equals the response's Last-Modified. Otherwise the full file is sent with 200. A route calling send_file without setting Last-Modified or ETag has nothing to compare, so a request carrying If-Range gets the full file there.
  • Close the connection after every refused WebSocket handshake, not only Kemal's own 403 and 405. Once the Origin and method checks passed, a wrong Sec-WebSocket-Version (426) or a missing Sec-WebSocket-Key (400) was answered by Crystal's HTTP::WebSocketHandler without Connection: close, so with Connection: keep-alive, Upgrade a request pipelined behind the handshake was served: GET /chat with Sec-WebSocket-Version: 1337 followed by GET /internal got 426 and then 200 OK with the internal response. Kemal now refuses both itself with Connection: close (the 426 still carries Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13), after the Origin check, and the pipelined request is never read. Completes the fix for GHSA-gvhf-4v24-f8r5.

The FLARE team's open-source tool to identify capabilities in executable files.

This release fixes a security issue in how capa loads vivisect workspaces, a large batch of bug fixes, a new --reproducible flag for freeze, dependency updates, and 12 new rules. We'd like to thank the following contributors: Ange Albertini (@corkamig), @aryanyk, Luca Schrott (@1337Name), @eversinc33, Matt Williams (@mwilliams31), Rizky Mirzaviandy Priambodo (@Xavrir), Sukesh Kumar (@SkxOverKill), lakshit verma (@vee1e), @w3lld1, and others!

Security

Crafted .viv files could execute code when capa analyzed a sample: either the sample itself named *.viv, or a <sample>.viv next to it. capa now always parses samples as PE or ELF and only loads an existing <sample>.viv when CAPA_LOAD_VIV_WORKSPACE=1 is set. Only enable this for .viv files you trust.

Affected: v9.4.0 and earlier.

Note that the node tag feature in 2.6.0 was a technically semver-breaking change even though it is a backwards-compatible / non-breaking change in the meta-grammar. There may be similar non-breaking changes to the meta-grammar between minor versions in the future. These non-breaking changes, however, may translate into semver-breaking changes due to the additional variants propagated from the generated Rule enum.

This new feature caused issues in some Cargo version resolution situations where Cargo mixed different versions of pest dependencies. For this reason, these "grammar non-breaking but semver-breaking" changes are now available only under the "grammar-extras" feature flag. If you would like to use node tags (or other future grammar features), you can do so by enabling this flag on the pest_derive crate in your Cargo.toml:

...
pest_derive = { version = "2.9", features = ["grammar-extras"] }

item.title: [influxdata/influxdb] v3.12.1 | 10-14-26
item.description:
influxdata/influxdb | 31768 stars| 3724 forks.

| Shell | Rust | Dockerfile | Python | Answer Set Programming |

Scalable datastore for metrics, events, and real-time analytics

The following are some highlighted updates with the newest release for InfluxDB 3. Learn more via our full Release Notes.

Updates

Core

Features

  • Faster startup after large file removals: At startup, the files that snapshots and checkpoints mark as removed are now dropped from each table's file list in one pass. Previously, every removed file scanned the table's whole file list, so startup slowed sharply after many files were removed from a large table.

Bug fixes

  • Catalog failed to load after upgrading to v3.12.0: The server now loads a catalog in which a table has more than one field family with the same automatically generated name. Core releases before v3.10.0 and Enterprise releases before v3.9.0 could write such names when fields were added to an existing table. v3.12.0 rejected them, so a node with an affected catalog failed to start.
  • Acknowledged writes lost after a forced snapshot and a restart: WAL flushes now run one at a time. Previously, a forced Parquet snapshot, triggered by write buffer memory or --force-snapshot-max-age, could run while an earlier WAL file was still being written, and recorded that file as covered before its rows reached the buffer. If the node restarted before the next snapshot, it skipped that file and the acknowledged writes in it were lost.
  • Overwrites lost across snapshots: When two Parquet files hold the same time window because it was persisted across two snapshots, a point in the later file now wins over a point with the same series and timestamp in the earlier file. Previously, the earlier file could win, so a query returned the value from before the overwrite.
  • Failed streaming queries returned 200: A query in CSV, JSON, or JSON Lines format that fails before it returns any rows, such as a sort that exceeds the memory limit, now returns the error status and message. Previously, the server sent 200 and then dropped the connection, so clients saw an empty body and a transport error. An error after the first rows still ends the response early.
  • Writes near the maximum timestamp: A line with a timestamp later than 2262-04-11T23:39:59.999999999Z is now rejected with a 400 error. Previously, a timestamp that close to the maximum could panic the WAL flush when the server forced a snapshot.
  • system.parquet_files listed files under the wrong tables: A query on system.parquet_files without a table_name filter now lists only the tables in the current database. Previously, it could list the current database's files under the names of tables in other databases that had the same table ID.
  • Other bug fixes and performance improvements

Enterprise

All Core updates are included in Enterprise.
Additional Enterprise-specific updates:

Features

  • Larger bulk import batches (upgraded storage engine): The new --compactor-import-batch-size option sets the largest batch of staged data that one bulk import merge reads at once. The default is 4gb and is configurable up to one quarter of --compactor-input-size-budget.
  • Faster ingest node startup with many snapshots (upgraded storage engine): An ingest node no longer reads every snapshot manifest in object storage at startup. Previously, it read them all, so startup time grew with the number of manifests. The first start on v3.12.1 still reads every manifest once. system.pt_ingest_files now lists the files from the newest manifest plus the snapshots taken since the node started.
  • Faster compaction I/O (Parquet engine): The compactor now uploads a finished output file while it encodes the next one, and checks up to 8 input files at a time. Previously, it did both one file at a time.
  • WAL flush wait metric (Parquet engine): The new influxdb3_parquet_wal_flush_lock_wait_seconds histogram reports how long a WAL flush waited for an earlier flush to finish. The kind label is timed for the regular flush interval and forced for a flush that forces a snapshot.

Bug fixes

  • Missing rows after changing a table's file index columns (Parquet engine): The file index now records which columns each compacted generation indexed. A query that filters on a column that only some generations indexed scans the other generations instead of skipping them. Previously, after you added or removed file index columns, such a query could return incomplete results from compacted data.
  • Overwrites reverted to the older value (upgraded storage engine): When the ingest buffer merges new writes into data it already merged for the same time window, a later write now wins over an earlier write to the same series and timestamp. Previously, the earlier value could replace the later one.
  • Storage engine upgrade failed with more than one compact node: During an upgrade to the upgraded storage engine, only the compact node that holds the compactor lease now drives the upgrade. Previously, every compact node drove it at the same time, their progress updates conflicted, and the upgrade could be marked as failed.
  • Compactor replanned forever against a missing data file (upgraded storage engine): A run set whose data file is confirmed gone from object storage is now skipped after three failed compaction attempts, so planning moves on to other work. Previously, the compactor planned the same compaction on every pass, and it failed every time. Skipped run sets are counted in influxdb3_compactor_skipped_run_sets with reason="auto_data_file_not_found". Compactions of new snapshots and imports aren't covered.
  • Bulk import could stall object storage requests (upgraded storage engine): The server no longer leaves object storage requests unfinished while it checks the status of uploaded imports. Previously, during a credential refresh, one of those requests could hold the object store client's credential lock and never release it, so every other request on the node waited behind it: the server stayed up but stopped reading from and writing to object storage.
  • Nodes without query mode built an unused file index (Parquet engine): Only nodes that run in query mode, including all, now load the compacted data file index at startup. Previously, compact and process nodes also loaded it, which used startup time and memory for an index they never read. A node that skips the index logs compacted-data file index not loaded.
  • Ingest node refused to restart after an unclean stop (Parquet engine): An ingest node that stopped without a clean shutdown now starts again. Previously, if a snapshot covered all of its WAL or a forced snapshot ran during startup, the node could fail every start with an error that it was still running in another process, though no other process existed.
  • Other bug fixes and performance improvements

egui: an easy-to-use immediate mode GUI in Rust that runs on both web and native


egui is an easy-to-use immediate mode GUI for Rust that runs on both web and native.

Try it now: https://www.egui.rs/

egui development is sponsored by Rerun, a startup building an SDK for visualizing streams of multimodal data.

Highlights ✨

Emoji and glyph support

egui can now render any glyph that is supported on your system, including colored emojis and non-Latin scripts.

To enable this, the integration has to use one of two APIs:

  • Context::add_glyph_rasterizer(GlyphRasterizer): a GlyphRasterizer renders a single glyph. eframe uses this on web to render individual glyphs to an off-screen canvas #8490, #8545.
  • Context::add_font_provider(Arc<dyn FontProvider>): lets egui find and load whole fonts at runtime. Native eframe uses this through the new egui_system_font_provider crate, which lists system fonts with fontique #8512.

Completion popup

We've added a new CompletionPopup widget that adds autocomplete to a TextEdit.
You can use it e.g. to add emoji selection like in discord:

Screen.Recording.2026-10-15.at.16.05.41.mov

Experimental theme customizations

This release adds a theme plugin system #8153 by @AdrienZianne. Enable the new experimental feature flag, and there will be a
new StyleProvider trait, which can be used to customize visuals for a widget based on the provided classes.

/// Implement the trait for each Widget you'd like to customize
impl StyleProvider<ButtonStyle> for MyTheme {
  fn style(&mut self, args: &StyleArgs<'_>) -> ButtonStyle {
    // You could construct ButtonStyle from scratch, or extend eguis built in style:
    let mut style: ButtonStyle = DefaultStyle.style(args);
    if args.has_class("primary") {
      style.atom_layout.frame.fill = hex_color!("#FF0000");
    }
    style
  }
}

/// Register all your custom style providers
fn init(ctx: &Context) {
  ctx.add_widget_theme::<ButtonStyle>(MyTheme);
  ctx.add_widget_theme::<CheckboxStyle>(MyTheme);
  // ...
}

Record videos of integration tests

Reading an integration test to understand what its doing can be challenging, so we've added a egui_kittest/video
feature that records a mp4 video from it, using ffmpeg! Enable it and pass EGUI_KITTEST_RECORD=1 or EGUI_KITTEST_RECORD=open,
and a video of the test will be recorded. This is an example from one of our more complex rerun integration tests:
